# Domain Rules

<!-- Generated by /ai-context. Manual edits are overwritten on re-run. -->

## AS IS — Current state

### Overview

- Two lead contexts: **global** (visitor picks a subject) and **produto** (visitor arrives via a product trigger, subject is forced) (`src/core/context.js`).
- Brazilian WhatsApp phone normalization/validation to the `55` country-code + 10-11 digit shape (`src/core/phone.js`).
- Form validation with a bot honeypot short-circuit (`src/core/validation.js`).
- Lead payload shaping — different required fields depending on context (`src/core/payload.js`).
- Traffic-origin attribution from UTM params, referrer, or a configurable default (`src/core/context.js:getTrafficOrigin`).
- WhatsApp message text generation from the payload (`src/core/whatsapp.js`).

### Rule: Product vs global context detection

- `readProductContext(element, win)` returns `null` unless the trigger element has **both** non-empty `data-product-name` and `data-product-id` (`.trim()`ed) — a trigger missing either attribute falls back to the global flow with manual subject selection, confirmed by README: "Se `data-product-name` ou `data-product-id` estiverem ausentes, o widget usa o fluxo global."
- Implementing file: `src/core/context.js:readProductContext`.
- Consumed in `src/ui/widget.js:attachProductTriggers` — click handler picks `readProductContext(trigger, win) || createGlobalContext(win)`.

### Rule: Name validation

- Valid name = at least 2 whitespace-separated parts, each part length ≥ 2 characters, after `.trim()` and collapsing repeated whitespace (`/\s+/`).
- Implementing file: `src/core/validation.js:validateName`.
- Error message on failure: `'Informe seu nome completo.'`.

### Rule: Brazilian WhatsApp phone normalization/validation

| Step | Behavior | Function |
|---|---|---|
| Strip non-digits | `value.replace(/\D/g, '')` | `onlyDigits` |
| Strip leading `00` (international dial prefix) | `digits.slice(2)` if `digits.startsWith('00')` | `normalizeWhatsapp` |
| Prepend country code | prepend `'55'` only if digits do NOT already start with `55` AND length is exactly 10 or 11 | `normalizeWhatsapp` |
| Validate | regex `^55\d{10,11}$` (55 + 10 or 11 digits: DDD + 8/9-digit number) | `isValidBrazilianWhatsapp` |
| Format for display | `(DD) NNNNN-NNNN` (11 digits) or `(DD) NNNN-NNNN` (10 digits), progressively built while typing | `formatPhoneForDisplay` |

- Implementing file: `src/core/phone.js`.
- Bound live to the `whatsapp` input via `input` event in `src/ui/widget.js:bindEvents` (formats as the visitor types).
- Error message on invalid: `'Informe um WhatsApp valido com DDD.'` (`src/core/validation.js`).

### Rule: Form validation order and honeypot bot block

Order of checks in `validateLeadForm(values, { subjects })` (`src/core/validation.js`):

| Order | Check | Failure result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `honeypot` field (`company_url` by default, `config.honeypotName`) non-empty after trim | Immediate return `{ valid: false, bot: true, errors: { honeypot: 'Envio bloqueado.' } }` — skips all other checks |
| 2 | `validateName(name)` | `errors.name` |
| 3 | `isValidBrazilianWhatsapp(whatsapp)` | `errors.whatsapp` |
| 4 | `lgpdAccepted` truthy | `errors.lgpd` |
| 5 | subject required **only when** `values.productContext` is falsy — `isValidSubject(subject, subjects)` checks membership in the configured subject list (default `['Dúvida técnica', 'Pedidos', 'Cadastro', 'Outros']`, `src/config.js:GLOBAL_SUBJECTS`) | `errors.subject` |

- Result: `{ valid: Object.keys(errors).length === 0, bot: false, errors }`.
- Consumed in `src/ui/widget.js:submit` — `validation.bot` returns `REGISTRATION_STATUS.HONEYPOT_ABORT` without calling the webhook or opening WhatsApp; `!validation.valid` shows joined error messages and aborts submission.

### Rule: Lead payload shape (context-dependent required fields)

| Context | Required-shape fields (`hasRequiredPayloadShape`) | Extra fields |
|---|---|---|
| Global | `nome`, `whatsapp` (matches `^55\d{10,11}$`), `origem_trafego`, `url_origem`, `data_hora`, AND `assunto` ∈ `['Duvida tecnica', 'Pedidos', 'Cadastro']` (note: hardcoded ASCII list in `hasRequiredPayloadShape`, distinct from the accented `GLOBAL_SUBJECTS` list used for form validation) | `assunto` |
| Produto | same base fields, AND `produto_interesse` + `produto_id` both truthy | `produto_interesse`, `produto_id` |

- Implementing file: `src/core/payload.js:buildLeadPayload`, `hasRequiredPayloadShape`.
- `buildLeadPayload` branches on `input.productContext?.productName && input.productContext?.productId` — if both present, sets `produto_interesse`/`produto_id` and omits `assunto`; otherwise sets `assunto = input.subject`.
- `getLeadTopic(payload)` returns `produto_interesse` if present, else `assunto`, else `''` — used to build the WhatsApp message topic.
- To extend: add a new context type by (1) extending `context.js` to produce it, (2) branching in `buildLeadPayload` for its fields, (3) updating `hasRequiredPayloadShape`'s topic check.

### Rule: Traffic origin attribution

Precedence in `getTrafficOrigin(win, defaultOrigin)` (`src/core/context.js`):

| Priority | Source | Value |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | UTM query params present (`utm_source`, `utm_medium`, or `utm_campaign`) | `[source, medium, campaign].filter(Boolean).join(' / ')` |
| 2 | `document.referrer` non-empty | raw referrer string |
| 3 | fallback | `config.defaultOrigin` (default `'Site'`, `src/config.js:DEFAULT_CONFIG.defaultOrigin`) |

### Rule: WhatsApp message text generation

| Payload state | Message template | Function |
|---|---|---|
| No `nome` | `Ola! Gostaria de atendimento sobre {topic}.` (or `'Ola! Gostaria de atendimento.'` if no topic) | `buildWhatsappMessage` |
| Has `nome` | `Ola! Me chamo {nome} e gostaria de atendimento sobre {topic}. Podem me ajudar? Vim pelo site. (Ref: {origem_trafego}).` | `buildWhatsappMessage` |

- Implementing file: `src/core/whatsapp.js:buildWhatsappMessage`, `buildWhatsappUrl` (URL-encodes the message and builds `https://wa.me/{normalizeWhatsapp(phoneNumber)}?text={message}`).
- `disableForm: true` mode skips the form entirely — `LeadWidget.open()` builds a payload with only `origin`, `sourceUrl`, `date`, and product context (no `nome`, no `whatsapp` capture), so the "no `nome`" template branch always fires (`src/ui/widget.js:open`).

### Rule: Webhook registration outcome (non-blocking on redirect)

| Condition | `status` | Blocks WhatsApp redirect? |
|---|---|---|
| Missing `webhookUrl` or no fetch implementation | `falha_tratada` (`reason: 'missing_webhook'`) | No |
| `fetch` resolves `response.ok` | `sucesso` | No |
| `fetch` resolves non-ok | `falha_tratada` (`reason: 'http_error'`) | No |
| `fetch` throws `AbortError` (timeout, default 3000ms) | `falha_tratada` (`reason: 'timeout'`) | No |
| `fetch` throws any other error | `falha_tratada` (`reason: 'network_error'`) | No |
| Honeypot triggered | `abortado_honeypot` | Yes — submission aborts before webhook/redirect (`src/ui/widget.js:submit`) |

- Implementing file: `src/integrations/webhook.js:postLead`, `REGISTRATION_STATUS`.
- The widget always proceeds to `pushGtmEvent` + `buildWhatsappUrl` + redirect regardless of webhook outcome (except the honeypot case) — `src/ui/widget.js:submit` shows `'Abrindo WhatsApp...'` on success or `'Abrindo WhatsApp mesmo assim...'` on failure, but redirects either way.
